description:
From the fz-kdt.107 census, RE-TARGETED by the fz-kdt.125 cold review
(2026-09-01): 13 (re-measured; was 12) of the corpus's runtime-
indistinguishable groups are the closure-identity shape --
discriminating_inputs finds nothing, the plan emits ZERO tests, source
order routes everything to arm 0, and arms 1..n are provably
unreachable yet fully specialized, lowered, and shipped.

RESOLUTION (settled by the 125 review): NOT 'never mint the arms' (the
generalization cure was prototyped and refuted -- 7 fixture breaks, 16
lib gates) but 'MAKE THE ARMS LIVE': fz-kdt.125's closure-identity
predicate axis gives each of the 13 groups a real runtime question
(13/13 separable by fn id alone, census-measured), so the arms become
reachable and the specializations stop being dead. The earlier
inventory-drop expectation is WITHDRAWN. The 'callable correlation is
runtime-unobservable' policy statement in this ticket's earlier body
and in callsite_dispatch.rs:146 is refuted by the runtime
representation (identity at closure_ptr+8 on all three paths) and its
deletion rides with the 125 build. AFTER 125 lands: re-run the census
helper; this ticket closes when the no-question population is zero (or
each survivor is fz-kdt.127's same-fn-id shape, which the diagnostic
backstop owns). Blocked by fz-kdt.125.

comments.text:
fz-kdt.125 LANDED (2026-09-01). Re-run of the census helper against the landed
callable axis: no-question dispatch groups 13 -> 6, fixtures carrying them
9 -> 5. This ticket does NOT close at zero, and the reason is measured, not
deferred: the helper's "separable by closure-literal identity" count was
regexing closure names out of CAPTURES as well as out of identity positions.
All six survivors are fz-kdt.127's same-fn-id shape (one lambda closed over two
different inner callables), which no identity axis can separate. See the
fz-kdt.127 comment for the per-fixture table.

The arms that WERE separable did become live, and two of them came back as
executables: enum_predicate_search 203 -> 204 and enum_reduce_halt_arm_order
+1, each an arm fz-kdt.118 had dropped as "runtime-indistinguishable and
strictly contained" that is no longer indistinguishable. Classified base vs
head across the whole corpus: zero pre-existing key, demand or transport line
changed text; the only additions are those two executables' own lines and eight
dispatch plans gaining callable-identity tests. Corpus stdout is byte-identical
on all 580 fixtures.

The refuted "callable correlation is runtime-unobservable" claim is gone from
callsite_dispatch.rs (the whole DispatchAlternative struct went with it), from
.agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md, and from behavior/enum_reduce_halt_arm_order.fz.
The permanent gate for the residue is
`compiler2_runtime_indistinguishable_arm_residue_stays_pinned`.

fz-kdt.119 review confirmation (2026-09-01): the +42 executable delta on three receive_* fixtures (dbg specs 1->8 per function, the 2^arity per-position product) is this ticket's arms-become-LIVE at scale, now measured. The specialization-count pressure is handed to fz-3bb with the mechanism recorded in fz-kdt.119's body.

CLOSED by fz-kdt.127.1 (2026-09-02): the no-question dispatch population is ZERO. The six same-fn-id/different-capture survivors (00231, 00277 x2, 00281, opaque_fn_value_join, repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2) gained construction-shape questions when the callable axis started naming captures; the INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_RESIDUE table was deleted and its fixtures promoted into the zero gate (compiler2_dispatch_offers_no_runtime_indistinguishable_arm). Arms became live, as this ticket predicted; then fz-kdt.127.2 removed most of those dispatches entirely by answering them at the key (net -52 runtime questions corpus-wide).

title: 12 no-question dispatch groups: the resolution is arms that BECOME LIVE, not arms never minted
